Shakespeare shaped history as much as he recorded it. His plays gave us murderous Macbeth, Caesar's famous last words, and a villainous hunchbacked Richard III. But how much was dramatic invention? From fabricated speeches to shuffled timelines, the Bard prioritised storytelling over accuracy, creating enduring myths we still believe today.
